about: D38 (decision log): the paired, interleaved confirmation that is the verdict on "no latency regression", on the scaling report's 300,000-patient snapshot (the kept D34 build, reused unchanged), by tools/benchmark_matcher.py --paired-confirm (protocol paired-interleaved-1.0) into a scratch report and committed here as it was written. The reference is main before D38 (e682817, extracted from git); the candidate is this tree, whose files the artifact digests bind. The matcher comparison report is not regenerated (nothing it binds changed). The confirmation queries carry no gene step, and the snapshot holds no gene label, so this measures the path every request without a gene step takes; execution_store.py and store_conditions_relative.py are byte-identical in the two codes. Latency of gene requests at scale is not measured.
rule: No latency regression: at 14 workers the paired p95 ratio (candidate over reference) is at most 1.05 in every pair, and the candidate's own 14-worker p95 is at most 10 s; the 8-worker figures are reported (committed in a26f821).

paired_confirmation.order: ABBA: the reference first in even repeats, the candidate first in odd
paired_confirmation.note: Each pair is the reference code and the candidate code run back to back, each in a fresh process with a warm pool, on the same snapshot and queries; the reference runs first in even repeats and second in odd ones (ABBA). Ratios are candidate over reference: below 1 means the candidate is faster. "total" is the sum of the per-query match seconds of one run. The absolute target is judged on the candidate's own runs in this session. The pairing cancels drift that is slow against the length of a pair (minutes); it does not cancel noise within a run, nor a difference that only one order shows (compare the reference-first and candidate-first pairs).

limitations: one machine and one session; synthetic data replicated beyond 10,000 patients; the p95 of 30 queries is the second-slowest query; the paired protocol cancels slow drift, not noise inside a run; no gene request is timed
